source_refs.note: Book p. 25: 2.1.4 Types of Function: (i) one-to-one, (ii) onto, (iii) bijective, Piecewise Function with its graph.
Book p. 26: Examples 5-6 with the graph of f(x) = x^2 - 2. Teaching notes, Exam tips, Key points and Common mistake are ours.

blocks.text: Ab tak hum ne yeh dekha ke koi rule function hai ya nahin. Aaj hum ek qadam aage jayenge: functions ki qisamein. Har function mein har input ka ek output hota hai, yeh to tay hai. Lekin sawal yeh hai: kya do inputs ka output same ho sakta hai? Kya co-domain ka har element kisi na kisi ka output banta hai? In do sawalon ke jawab se teen ahem qisamein banti hain: one-to-one, onto aur bijective. Aakhir mein piecewise function bhi dekhenge.
(i) One-to-One (Injective) Function

Kitab kehti hai: function \(f\) one-to-one hai agar mukhtalif inputs mukhtalif outputs dein, yani agar \(f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2})\) se \(x_{1} = x_{2}\) nikle. Matlab domain ke koi do alag elements co-domain ke ek hi element par nahin jate.
Misaal ke tor par \(f(x) = 5x + 7\) one-to-one hai, kyun ke \(5x_{1} + 7 = 5x_{2} + 7\) se \(x_{1} = x_{2}\) nikalta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab ki misaal mein do chhote steps chhoot gaye hain; woh yeh hain. Dono taraf se \(7\) tafreeq karein, phir \(5\) se taqseem karein:
\[5x_{1} + 7 = 5x_{2} + 7\]
\[5x_{1} = 5x_{2}\]
\[x_{1} = x_{2}\]
One-to-one saabit karne ka tareeqa: maan lein \(f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2})\), phir algebra se dikhayein ke \(x_{1} = x_{2}\). Yani "agar output barabar hain to input bhi barabar the".
Ghalat saabit karne ka tareeqa: sirf do aise alag inputs dhoond lein jin ka output same ho. Ek hi counter-example (ulti misaal) kaafi hai.
Roz marra ki misaal: "student \(\to\) roll number" one-to-one hai (do students ka ek roll number nahin hota), lekin "student \(\to\) qad" one-to-one nahin, kyun ke do students ka qad barabar ho sakta hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Graph par one-to-one check karne ke liye horizontal (leti hui) line istemal karein: function one-to-one hai agar koi bhi horizontal line us ke graph ko ek se zyada dafa na kaate. Isay vertical line test (2.1.3) se mila kar yaad rakhein: vertical line batati hai ke graph function hai ya nahin; horizontal line batati hai ke woh one-to-one hai ya nahin.

One-to-one ne inputs ki taraf se dekha tha: kya do inputs takra to nahin rahe? Ab onto co-domain ki taraf se dekhta hai: kya co-domain ka har element kisi na kisi input ka output bana? Yeh do bilkul alag sawal hain, is liye in dono ko kabhi gadmad na karein.
(ii) Onto (Surjective) Function

Kitab kehti hai: function \(f : X \to Y\) ko onto (ya surjective) kehte hain agar co-domain \(Y\) ke har element ki domain \(X\) mein kam az kam ek pre-image ho. Doosre lafzon mein, \(Y\) ke har \(y\) ke liye \(X\) mein koi \(x\) aisa ho ke \(f(x) = y\).

Misaal: \(f(x) = 2x + 3\), jahan domain aur co-domain dono real numbers hain. Yahan
\[y = 2x + 3\]
\[\Rightarrow x = \dfrac{y - 3}{2}\]
\[f\left(\dfrac{y - 3}{2}\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{y - 3}{2}\right) + 3 = y\]
\(\mathbb{R}\) ke har \(y\) ke liye \(\mathbb{R}\) mein \(\frac{y - 3}{2}\) maujood hai jis ka output \(y\) hai. Is liye \(f\) onto function hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pre-image ka matlab: woh input \(x\) jis ka output \(y\) ho. Yani \(y\) ka "pichla" ya "asal" number. Onto ka matlab hai: range = co-domain, yani co-domain ka koi element bekaar nahin reh jata, har ek tak koi na koi teer pahunchta hai.
Onto saabit karne ka tareeqa (jaise upar \(2x + 3\) mein kiya): co-domain ka koi bhi \(y\) lein, \(y = f(x)\) ko \(x\) ke liye hal karein, dekhein ke yeh \(x\) domain mein hai, aur phir \(f(x) = y\) kar ke tasdeeq karein.
Dhyan dein: onto hona co-domain par depend karta hai. \(f(x) = x^{2}\), \(\mathbb{R}\) se \(\mathbb{R}\) tak, onto nahin (\(-1\) ki koi pre-image nahin, kyun ke koi square negative nahin hota). Lekin \(\mathbb{R}\) se \([0, \infty)\) tak yahi function onto hai.
(iii) Bijective Function
Kitab kehti hai: function \(f : X \to Y\) ko bijective kehte hain agar woh one-to-one bhi ho aur onto bhi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Bijective ko "poori jori" samjhiye: \(Y\) ka har element \(X\) ke bilkul ek element ka output hai. Onto "kam az kam ek" deta hai aur one-to-one "zyada se zyada ek"; dono mil kar "bilkul ek" ban jate hain. Jaise ek class mein har student ki ek kursi ho aur har kursi par ek student; na koi kursi khaali, na kisi kursi par do students.
Bijective saabit karne ke liye dono hisse alag alag saabit karne parte hain. Upar wale \(5x + 7\) aur \(2x + 3\), dono \(\mathbb{R}\) se \(\mathbb{R}\) tak bijective hain.

Ab ek bilkul naya andaaz dekhte hain. Ab tak har function ek hi formula se likha gaya tha. Lekin kabhi kabhi ek formula poore domain par theek kaam nahin karta, aur humein domain ke mukhtalif hisson par mukhtalif formulas lagane parte hain. Aise function ko piecewise function kehte hain.
Piecewise Function

Kitab kehti hai: piecewise function aisa function hai jo apne domain ke mukhtalif hisson (intervals) par mukhtalif expressions (ya "tukron") se define hota hai. Har tukra domain ke ek khaas hisse par lagta hai.
Misaal ke tor par,

blocks.text_alt: f of x equals 2 x plus 1 if x is less than 0, and x squared minus 1 if x is greater than or equal to 0

blocks.text: \(x < 0\) ke liye function \(2x + 1\) ki tarah chalta hai aur \(x \ge 0\) ke liye \(x^{2} - 1\) ki tarah. Roz marra ki misaal: bijli ka bill, jahan pehle 100 units ka rate ek hai aur us se upar ka rate doosra; yeh bhi piecewise rule hai.

blocks.alt: Graph on a grid, x from minus 4 to 4 and y from minus 3 to 3. For x less than 0 the straight line y = 2x + 1 rises from (minus 2, minus 3) to (0, 1). For x greater than or equal to 0 the curve y = x squared minus 1 starts at (0, minus 1), crosses the x-axis at (1, 0) and rises to (2, 3).
blocks.caption: Figure: the piecewise function f(x) = 2x + 1 for x < 0 and x² − 1 for x ≥ 0 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Piecewise function ki value nikalne ka tareeqa: pehle faisla karein ke input kis tukre mein aata hai, phir sirf wohi tukra use karein:
\(f(-2)\): \(-2 < 0\), is liye \(f(-2) = 2(-2) + 1 = -3\).
\(f(0)\): \(0 \ge 0\), is liye \(f(0) = 0^{2} - 1 = -1\).
\(f(2)\): \(2 \ge 0\), is liye \(f(2) = 2^{2} - 1 = 3\).
Graph mein line wala hissa \((0, 1)\) tak jata hai, lekin yeh point graph mein shaamil nahin: \(x = 0\) doosre tukre (piece) mein aata hai, jo \((0, -1)\) se shuru hota hai kyun ke \(f(0) = -1\). Har input ka phir bhi ek hi output hai, is liye piecewise function sacha function hai (vertical line test bhi pass karta hai).
Ab kitab ki do misaalein dekhte hain. Pehli mein hum ek function ko bijective saabit karenge (dono shartein poori), doosri mein dikhayenge ke ek function dono shartein tod deta hai.

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.problem: Show that the function \(f(x) = x + 1\), where the domain and co-domain are all real numbers, is bijective.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x + 1\), \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\).
To prove: \(f\) bijective hai.
Method: bijective ka matlab hai one-to-one aur onto dono. Is liye do alag hisse saabit karenge: pehle one-to-one, phir onto.

Hissa 1: one-to-one
Function one-to-one hai agar \(f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2}) \Rightarrow x_{1} = x_{2}\). Maan lein
\[f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2})\]
\[x_{1} + 1 = x_{2} + 1\]
\[\Rightarrow x_{1} = x_{2}\]
Is liye diya gaya function one-to-one hai.
Kyun: dono taraf se \(1\) tafreeq karne par \(x_{1} = x_{2}\) bachta hai. Yani barabar output sirf barabar inputs se aa sakte hain. Hum ne koi khaas number nahin liya, general \(x_{1}, x_{2}\) liye; is liye yeh har input ke liye saabit hua.

Hissa 2: onto
Koi bhi real number \(y\) lein. \(y = x + 1\) ko hal karein: \(x = y - 1\), jo real number hai.
\[f(y - 1) = y - 1 + 1 = y\]
Kyun: co-domain ke har \(y\) ki domain mein pre-image \(y - 1\) maujood hai. Yahi onto ki definition hai. Hum ne pehle \(x\) dhoonda, phir \(f(x)\) nikal kar dekha ke sach mein \(y\) aata hai.

Natija
\(f\) one-to-one bhi hai aur onto bhi, is liye \(f(x)\) bijective hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(y = 7\) lein: pre-image \(7 - 1 = 6\), aur \(f(6) = 7\). Sahi! Aur do alag inputs, maslan \(2\) aur \(5\), ke outputs \(3\) aur \(6\) hain, jo alag hain, jaisa one-to-one mein hona chahiye.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(f(x) = x + 1\) one-to-one aur onto hai, is liye bijective hai.

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem: Show that the function \(f(x) = x^{2} - 2\), where the domain and co-domain are all real numbers, is neither one-to-one nor onto.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{2} - 2\), \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\).
To prove: \(f\) na one-to-one hai na onto.
Method: kisi khoobi ko ghalat saabit karne ke liye ek counter-example kaafi hai. Do aise inputs dhoondenge jin ka output same ho, aur co-domain ka aisa element jis ki koi pre-image na ho.

One-to-one ki shart aazmaayein
\[f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2})\]
\[x_{1}^{2} - 2 = x_{2}^{2} - 2\]
\[x_{1}^{2} = x_{2}^{2}\]
Square root lene se \(x_{1} = x_{2}\) ya \(x_{1} = -x_{2}\).
Kyun: do numbers ka square tab barabar hota hai jab woh barabar hon ya ek doosre ke negative hon (\(3^{2} = (-3)^{2} = 9\)). Is liye barabar output se barabar input zaroori nahin nikalta.

Counter-example: one-to-one nahin
\(x_{1} = 2\), \(x_{2} = -2\), yani \(x_{1} \ne x_{2}\), aur
\[f(2) = 4 - 2 = 2\]
\[f(-2) = 4 - 2 = 2\]
Is liye \(f\) one-to-one nahin.
Kyun: do alag inputs ek hi output \(2\) de rahe hain (figure mein height 2 par dashed line dekhiye, jo parabola ko do jagah chhooti hai).

Onto nahin
\(x^{2} \ge 0\), is liye \(f(x) = x^{2} - 2 \ge -2\). \(f\) ki sab se chhoti value \(-2\) hai, aur woh sirf \(x = 0\) par aati hai.
Co-domain \(\mathbb{R}\) mein \(-2\) se chhota koi bhi number kisi real \(x\) ki image nahin. Maslan \(f(x) = -3\):
\[x^{2} - 2 = -3\]
\[x^{2} = -1\]
jis ka koi real root nahin.
Kyun: co-domain poora \(\mathbb{R}\) hai, lekin range sirf \([-2, \infty)\) hai; \(-3\) jaise elements ki koi pre-image nahin. Kisi real number ka square \(-1\) nahin ho sakta.

Tasdeeq:
Graph se dekhiye: horizontal line \(y = 2\) parabola ko do dafa kaat'ti hai (one-to-one nahin), aur parabola apne sab se neeche wale point \((0, -2)\) se neeche kabhi nahin jata (onto nahin).
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(f(x) = x^{2} - 2\) one-to-one nahin (\(f(2) = f(-2) = 2\)) aur onto bhi nahin (\(-3\) ki koi pre-image nahin).

blocks.alt: Graph of y = x squared minus 2 on a grid, x from minus 3 to 3 and y from minus 3 to 4, with lowest point (0, minus 2). The points (minus 2, 2) and (2, 2), labelled f(minus 2) = 2 and f(2) = 2, are joined by a dashed horizontal line, with dashed vertical lines down to x = minus 2 and x = 2.
blocks.caption: Figure: f(x) = x² − 2 takes the same value 2 at x = −2 and x = 2 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = 3x - 4\), \(\mathbb{R}\) se \(\mathbb{R}\) tak: kya yeh bijective hai?
Jawab: one-to-one: \(3x_{1} - 4 = 3x_{2} - 4 \Rightarrow x_{1} = x_{2}\). Onto: \(y = 3x - 4 \Rightarrow x = \frac{y + 4}{3}\), jo har real \(y\) ke liye real hai, aur \(f\left(\frac{y + 4}{3}\right) = y\). Is liye haan, bijective hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Ab \(g(x) = x^{2}\) ko \([0, \infty)\) se \([0, \infty)\) tak lein (yeh hamari practice hai). One-to-one: \(x_{1}^{2} = x_{2}^{2}\) se \(x_{1} = \pm x_{2}\), lekin dono non-negative hain, is liye \(x_{1} = x_{2}\). Onto: har \(y \ge 0\) ki pre-image \(\sqrt{y} \ge 0\). To yeh bijective hai! Sabaq: wahi formula, domain aur co-domain badalne se qisam badal jati hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. One-to-one: \(f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2}) \Rightarrow x_{1} = x_{2}\) (alag inputs, alag outputs).
2. Onto: co-domain ke har element ki kam az kam ek pre-image; range = co-domain.
3. Bijective: one-to-one aur onto dono.
4. Saabit karne ke liye general \(x_{1}, x_{2}\) ya general \(y\) lein; ghalat saabit karne ke liye ek counter-example kaafi hai.
5. Piecewise function mein pehle tukra chunein, phir value nikaalein.
6. Horizontal line test: graph ko koi horizontal line do dafa kaate to function one-to-one nahin.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Numbers se one-to-one saabit karna ("\(f(1) \ne f(2)\)"). Chand misaalein kabhi saboot nahin hotin; general \(x_{1}, x_{2}\) lein.
2. Onto saabit karte waqt yeh check na karna ke pre-image domain mein hai.
3. Co-domain dekhe baghair onto keh dena: \(x^{2}\), \([0, \infty)\) par onto hai lekin \(\mathbb{R}\) par nahin.
4. Piecewise function mein ek input par dono tukre laga dena, ya boundary \(x = 0\) par ghalat tukra lena (\(x = 0\) ke liye \(x \ge 0\) wala tukra, yani \(x^{2} - 1\)).
5. Open aur filled dot ka farq bhool jana.
